_meta.purpose: Volatile, sourced reference figures for the two LLM-application volumes. Every caveat is deliberate: a number without its date and source is a liability. Pages load this file at runtime and fall back to an inline FALLBACK if the fetch fails.
_meta.rule: If a figure can rot (a price, a context window, a benchmark score, a spec revision), it lives here with a `source` string carrying a date. If it cannot rot (BM25's formula, an algorithm's name), it lives in the prose.

context_windows.source: Vendor model cards and API docs, retrieved 2026-09. GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 (128K); Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet and Claude 4.x (200K, with 1M available on some tiers); Gemini 1.5 Pro (2M) and Gemini 2.x (1M); Llama 3.1/3.3 (128K); DeepSeek-V3 config max_position_embeddings 163,840, advertised 128K; Kimi K2 (128K); Qwen2.5 (128K). Windows move fast and several of these are already superseded; treat every value as a dated snapshot, not a current quote.

context_rot.source: Liu et al., 'Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts' (arXiv:2307.03172, TACL 2024) shows a U-shaped accuracy curve for information placed at the start, middle and end of a long context. Chroma's 'Context Rot' report (2025-07) measured degradation that begins well below the advertised window on many models. Exact degradation curves are model- and task-specific; the numbers here are illustrative of the shape, not universal constants.
context_rot.shape: U-shaped: best at the very start (primacy) and very end (recency), worst in the middle.
context_rot.caveat: Reasoning models and explicit instructions move the curve, but none eliminates the middle dip entirely.

pricing.source: HISTORICAL vendor list prices, early-to-mid 2025, per 1M tokens (USD, standard, non-batch). These rot fast and are labelled historical reference points, not current quotes. OpenAI GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini pricing pages (2024-2025); Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet (2024) and Claude 3.7 Sonnet (Feb 2025) at $3/$15 with cache read $0.30; Google Gemini 1.5 Flash and 2.0 Flash pricing pages; DeepSeek-V3 official API pricing Feb 2025 ($0.07 cache hit / $0.27 cache miss / $1.10 output). Verify against live vendor pages before relying on any number.
pricing.outputInputRatio: Output is the expensive side at every vendor in this table: 3x (GPT-4o), 5x (Claude), 4x (Gemini 1.5 Flash), 4x (DeepSeek-V3). The lever is almost always shortening the output, not the input.

prompt_cache.source: Anthropic prompt-caching docs (2024-08; 5-minute TTL, cache read 0.1x base input, cache write 1.25x) and OpenAI prompt-caching docs (2024-10; automatic for prompts over 1,024 tokens, cached input 0.5x, reported in `cached_tokens`). Google and DeepSeek publish equivalent implicit caches. Provider implementations differ in block size, TTL and eviction, so the hit rate is a property of your prompt layout, not the vendor.

retrieval_contextual.source: Anthropic, 'Introducing Contextual Retrieval' (2024-09-19). Reported top-20 retrieval failure rate on a large corpus falling from 5.7% (baseline) to 3.7% with contextual embeddings, 2.9% with contextual embeddings + BM25, and 1.9% with contextual embeddings + BM25 + reranking. Those are absolute failure rates; the widely quoted '35% -> 49% -> 67%' figures are the relative reductions in failure rate at each step. Corpus, chunking and reranker dependent.

embeddings.source: Sentence-BERT (Reimers & Gurevych, arXiv:1908.10084, EMNLP 2019); E5 (Wang et al., arXiv:2212.03533, 2022); BGE / C-Pack (Xiao et al., arXiv:2309.07597, 2023); Matryoshka Representation Learning (Kusupati et al., arXiv:2205.13147, NeurIPS 2022) for nested, truncatable embeddings; MTEB (Muennighoff et al., arXiv:2210.07316, 2022) as the leaderboard. MTEB scores are dominated by a handful of points and correlate imperfectly with retrieval on a specific corpus: treat the leaderboard as a shortlist, then measure on your own labelled set.
embeddings.matryoshkaTruncation: A Matryoshka-trained embedding can be truncated at 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 of its width with a small, measurable recall loss — cheaper storage and faster search in exchange for accuracy you can plot.

ann.source: HNSW (Malkov & Yashunin, arXiv:1603.09320, 2016/2018), IVF and product quantization (Jégou et al., arXiv:1102.3828, IEEE TPAMI 2011), ScaNN (Guo et al., arXiv:1908.10396, ICML 2020), DiskANN (Subramanya et al., NeurIPS 2019). Recall/latency/memory figures below are order-of-magnitude from these papers and common benchmarks; they are workload-, dimension- and hardware-dependent, so read them as the shape of the tradeoff rather than as constants.

methods.note: Brute force. The correct baseline to measure every approximation against.
Cluster into nlist cells, probe the nearest nprobe. Recall is bounded by whether the true neighbour's cell was probed.
Compress residuals into product-quantization codes. Trades recall for a large memory win; the compression error is the price.
Layered navigable graph. M sets the degree, efSearch sets the recall/latency dial at query time.
Graph designed to live on disk with one pass; scales to billions of vectors on a single node.

hnswDefaults.note: Common starting points; efSearch is the query-time recall/latency knob and does not require a rebuild.

fusion.source: Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack, Clarke & Buettcher, SIGIR 2009), k=60 as the paper's default. SPLADE (Formal et al., arXiv:2107.05720, SIGIR 2021) for learned sparse retrieval; ColBERT late interaction (Khattab & Zaharia, arXiv:2004.12832, SIGIR 2020) and ColBERTv2 (Santhanam et al., arXiv:2112.01488, 2021); MUVERA (arXiv:2405.19504, 2024) turns multi-vector ColBERT similarity into single-vector MIPS. Cross-encoders rerank far more accurately than they retrieve, which is why the standard shape is retrieve-wide then rerank-narrow.
patterns: ColBERT late interaction as a middle ground between bi- and cross-encoders

rag.source: RAGAS metrics (Es et al., arXiv:2309.15217, EACL 2024): faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision, context recall. Self-RAG (Asai et al., arXiv:2310.11511, ICLR 2024) and CRAG / Corrective RAG (Yan et al., arXiv:2401.15884, 2024) add self-critique; GraphRAG (Microsoft Research, 2024) targets global 'what themes run through this corpus' questions that flat chunk retrieval cannot answer; ColPali (Faysse et al., arXiv:2407.01449, 2024) retrieves over page images without OCR; HyDE (Gao et al., arXiv:2212.10496, 2022) generates a hypothetical answer to embed as the query; multi-query and step-back prompting widen or abstract the query. Component-level numbers are benchmark-specific and do not transfer directly.

failureModes.mode: Answer not grounded in the context
Retrieved but not used (middle of long context)

prompt and tool design; measure it, do not assume it

evals.source: SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., arXiv:2310.06770, ICLR 2024) and SWE-bench Verified (OpenAI, 2024-08, a 500-instance human-validated subset); τ-bench (Yao et al., arXiv:2406.12045, 2024) and τ²-bench (2025) for tool-agent-user interaction, which introduced pass^k; GAIA (Mialon et al., arXiv:2311.12983, 2023) for general assistant tasks; OSWorld (Xie et al., arXiv:2404.07972, 2024) for computer use; HELM (Liang et al., arXiv:2211.09110, 2022) for holistic multi-metric reporting. Public scores are contaminated by training-data leakage, scaffolding differences and harness version drift, which is why a public number is a weak predictor of your task.
evals.passKFormula: pass^k = fraction of tasks solved on all k independent attempts — the reliability counterpart to pass@k's capability measure.

benchmarks.caveat: scaffold- and harness-dependent; the agent's tooling contributes at least as much variance as the model

benchmarks.measures: tool-agent-user dialogue with a verifiable database end state
benchmarks.caveat: scores move with the user simulator; read the trajectory, not just the end state

benchmarks.name: OSWorld
benchmarks.caveat: environment version changes the score; pin it

tuning.source: LoRA (Hu et al., arXiv:2106.09685, ICLR 2022); QLoRA (Dettmers et al., arXiv:2305.14314, NeurIPS 2023); DPO (Rafailov et al., arXiv:2305.18290, NeurIPS 2023); KTO (Ethayarajh et al., arXiv:2402.01306, 2024); ORPO (Hong, Lee & Thorne, arXiv:2403.07691, 2024); GRPO introduced in DeepSeekMath (Shao et al., arXiv:2402.03300, 2024) and used at scale for DeepSeek-R1 (arXiv:2501.12948, 2025). RLVR (reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards) trains on programmatically checkable outcomes (a test passes, a tool call is valid). The value of fine-tuning is the labelled dataset you curated, which survives every base-model upgrade; the weights do not.

methods.note: Freezes the base weights; serve one base with many adapters.
Quantized base plus adapters; the common single-GPU path.
Direct preference optimization; no separate reward model.
Needs only a thumbs-up/down signal rather than pairs.
Odds-ratio preference optimization; avoids a separate SFT stage.
For reasoning and tool use where correctness is checkable; reward hacking is the main failure mode.

tuning.rewardHacking: A verifier that checks the final answer but not the reasoning invites shortcut policies: exploit the checker, not solve the task. Hold out verifiers and inspect traces.

security.source: Indirect prompt injection named and demonstrated by Greshake et al., arXiv:2302.12173 (2023). The 'lethal trifecta' framing (private data + untrusted content + an exfiltration channel) is Simon Willison (2025-06). Dual-LLM pattern: Willison (2023). CaMeL, capability-based information-flow control for agents: Debenedetti et al., arXiv:2503.18813 (2025). GCG adversarial suffixes: Zou et al., arXiv:2307.15043 (2023); PAIR: Chao et al., arXiv:2310.08419 (2023); AgentDojo, a dynamic attack/defence benchmark: Debenedetti et al., arXiv:2406.13352 (2024). OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications lists prompt injection as LLM01.
trifecta: an exfiltration channel (a network tool, a rendered image, a writable output)

defensePatterns.label: No defense
defensePatterns.note: Untrusted text and privileged tools share one context.

defensePatterns.label: Prompt hardening
defensePatterns.note: Instructions to ignore untrusted content. Raises the bar; does not close the hole.

defensePatterns.label: Rails / classifiers
defensePatterns.note: Input and output classifiers as defence in depth; bypassable by novel encodings.

defensePatterns.label: Dual-LLM quarantine
defensePatterns.note: A quarantined model reads untrusted content and may only emit structured data to the privileged model.

defensePatterns.label: Least privilege
defensePatterns.note: Break the trifecta: never put private data and untrusted content in the same context with a live exfiltration path.

defensePatterns.label: Capability information flow
defensePatterns.note: Capability tokens decide which values may influence which actions, independent of the text that carries them. Strongest single control; still leaves authorised-user intent unconstrained.

mcp.source: Model Context Protocol, introduced by Anthropic 2024-11-25 and donated to the Linux Foundation; spec revisions are dated (2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18). The 2026 revision streamlines the core toward a stateless request/response model with explicit session handles, so a server can scale horizontally without sticky state. Treat the specific revision and its date as checkable against modelcontextprotocol.io; clients and servers lag the spec by months. Skills: Anthropic, 'Agent Skills' (2025), with a SKILL.md file loaded in three stages — metadata always, instructions on invocation, resources on demand.
skillStages: instructions (SKILL.md body, loaded when the skill is invoked)
resources (scripts and files, loaded on demand)

agents.source: Anthropic, 'Effective context engineering for AI agents' (2025-09-29) for the write/select/compress/isolate taxonomy and 'Building effective agents' (2024-12) for the workflow-versus-agent split; Anthropic, 'How we built our multi-agent research system' (2025-06-13); Cognition, 'Don't Build Multi-Agents' (2025-06). Reliability compounding is arithmetic: 0.95^20 ≈ 0.36. Harness design: context folding, step budgets, loop detection, sandboxing and permission gates are now as load-bearing as the model.
agents.compactionTax: Compaction is lossy and adversarial: an evicted fact is indistinguishable from a fact that never existed, so the agent silently redoes work.

cost_latency.source: Latency definitions follow the serving guide (TTFT, TPOT, goodput). The agent-loop cost is arithmetic: each turn resends the whole prior context, so N turns with a growing history cost O(N^2) input tokens before caching. Cache discounts are vendor-specific (see prompt_cache). The voice budget figures are illustrative of realtime voice pipelines (500-1000 ms end-to-end is the commonly cited target, with turn detection contributing a large, variable share); treat them as a shape, not a spec.

benchmark_card.source: Dated reference card, retrieved 2026-09. Scores are deliberately omitted where they change weekly; the card records what each benchmark measures, how it is graded, and its main failure as a signal. Fill in live numbers from the leaderboards, with the date.

rows.caveat: narrow; hard to game and hard to generalise from
